title: Length channelizer: runtime-driven pad-shedding and sequence-channel routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a runtime component (Length Channelizer) that dynamically routes in-flight requests into sequence-length channels to minimize padding overhead and select attention/kernel implementations appropriate to each channel. The feature scopes: histogram-driven channel boundaries, pad-shedding tensor slicing before kernel invocation, attention kernel selector heuristics (prefill vs decode), and scheduler tie-ins so prefill/decoder phases are coalesced without violating latency SLOs.
background: Current runtime groups by coarse bucket sizes leading to excess padding when request sequence lengths vary. We have multiple optimized attention kernels with different memory/compute trade-offs depending on sequence length and KV cache patterns. Prefill vs decode phases have different ideal batching strategies; naive coalescing either hurts decode tail latency or wastes compute with padded tokens. This ticket unifies a runtime layer that shapes micro-batches by sequence-length channels and emits per-channel kernel hints to the scheduler.
goals: Reduce average padding tokens per batch by >= 35% on mixed-webchat workload
Improve cost-per-token (GPU FLOP) by >= 18% for common customer mixes
Maintain p95 decode latency within current SLO (+5% tolerance) during rollout
Provide deterministic kernel-selection rules and observable metrics for each channel
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration test shows pad tokens reduced >= 35% on synthetic mixed-length trace
Kernel selector chooses short-seq kernel for channels with median seq_len <= 64 and long-seq kernel for median > 512
No customer-facing errors introduced; fallback to generic kernel on OOM or missing kernel available
Dashboard with per-channel token counts, pad ratio, chosen kernel, and p95 latency is shipping to Console
Feature gated behind runtime-length-channelizer FF; rollout steps documented
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike complete. Microbench harness shows pad reduction of ~40% using three-channel scheme on internal chat traces.
2026-02-22: Implemented channel boundary estimator (median+P75 based) and integrated metric emissions for pad_ratio per channel.
2026-02-26: Prototype kernel selector added: heuristic prefers 'short-attn' when median_seq <= 64 and avg_kvcache_hits < 0.2; empirical tuning pending.

2026-03-01: Scheduler hooks merged to allow prefill grouping separate from decode grouping; initial canary flagged for internal test cluster. Observed p95 decode increase of ~3% on heavy decode bursts — within tolerance.
implementation_notes: Channelization is performed at request enqueue time; requests annotated with seq_len and 'phase' tag (prefill|decode) to avoid mixing incompatible KV patterns.
Use histogram sketch (t-digest) per minute to adapt channel boundaries instead of static bins to handle diurnal traffic shifts.
Before kernel dispatch, perform pad-shedding: allocate compacted tensors containing only real tokens plus an index map for rehydration of outputs to original request shapes.
Kernel selection table maps (channel_id, phase, median_seq) -> preferred kernel variant; table stored in config and hot-reloadable.
Fallback policy: on OOM or kernel mismatch, fall back to safe-generic kernel and emit 'channel_fallback' metric.
Attention optimization: for short channels use fused QKV + rotary kernel; for long channels prefer sliced attention with sparse KV prefetch to reduce peak memory.
Avoid over-sharding: introduce jitter when forming channel batches to prevent pathological alignment causing head-of-line latency spikes.
Quantization/packed weights: ensure kernel ABI compatibility checks before routing; invalid combos should not be selected.
Expose per-request header to downstream tracing with channel_id and chosen_kernel for debugging.
Edge-case: streaming requests with unknown final length will be assigned to 'streaming' channel and use conservative kernel; add future work to allow dynamic migrate-on-prefill completion.
testing_plan: Unit tests for channel boundary estimator and histogram updates
Microbench suites comparing pad_ratio, memory footprint, and kernel throughput across channels
Integration tests with prefills and streaming decodes ensuring rehydration correctness
Chaos test: force kernel OOMs to validate fallback path and metrics
Canary in internal CI cluster with a 5% traffic slice and synthetic mixed-length traffic for 48 hours
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable FF on internal cluster; run 48h canary; monitor pad_ratio and p95 metrics
Phase 2 (opt-in customers): enable for select customers with high variance seq_len workloads; collect cost and latency signals
Phase 3 (global gradual): ramp feature gate across regions over 2 weeks with automated rollback if p95 increases > 10% or pad_ratio worsens
Final: enable by default and remove FF after 4 weeks of stable metrics
